questions.title: Calculating a Mean from Raw Decimal Data

parts.text:
Seven plant heights, in cm, are:
$$4.2,\; 5.1,\; 6.3,\; 4.8,\; 5.6,\; 6.0,\; 4.9$$
Calculate the mean height, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Finding a Missing Value from the Mean

parts.text:
Eight quiz scores have a mean of $14$. Seven of the scores are $11,\; 13,\; 15,\; 12,\; 16,\; 14,\; 16$.
Find the eighth quiz score.

Group $A$ consists of $8$ values with a mean of $14.5$. Group $B$ consists of $12$ values with a mean of $17.0$.
Calculate the combined mean of all $20$ values.

questions.title: Class Midpoints for Continuous Grouped Data

parts.text:
For the continuous grouped classes $0 \le t < 10$, $10 \le t < 20$, $20 \le t < 30$, and $30 \le t < 50$:
(i) state the midpoint of each class,
(ii) explain why the midpoint of the last class is $40$ rather than $35$.

questions.title: Recovering Class Frequencies from Cumulative Frequencies

parts.text:
The cumulative frequencies for classes with upper boundaries $10,\; 20,\; 40,\; 70$ are $6,\; 15,\; 27,\; 32$ respectively (where the variable starts at $0$).
Determine the individual class frequency for each of the four intervals.

questions.title: Why Grouped Mean is an Estimate

parts.text: Explain why the value calculated using $\frac{\sum f x}{\sum f}$ for grouped continuous data is an estimate of the true mean rather than an exact value.

questions.title: Combined Mean of Two Sports Squads

parts.text:
Nine basketball players have a mean height of $168\text{ cm}$. Eleven other players have a mean height of $174\text{ cm}$.
Calculate the total height of all 20 players.
Hence find the mean height of all 20 players, and explain why the combined mean is closer to 174 cm than to 168 cm.

questions.title: Weighted Mean from a Grouped Frequency Table

parts.text:
The times, $t$ minutes, taken by 20 students to complete an assignment are grouped as follows:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Time } (t \text{ minutes}) & \text{Frequency } (f) \\ \hline 0 \le t < 10 & 4 \\ 10 \le t < 20 & 7 \\ 20 \le t < 30 & 5 \\ 30 \le t < 50 & 4 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
State the midpoint of each of the four classes.
Calculate $\sum f x$ and hence calculate an estimate of the mean time taken by the students.

questions.title: Recovering an Unknown Price Using the Mean

parts.text:
A student purchases $6$ identical notebooks at $4.50\text{ dollars}$ each, $3$ identical folders, and $1$ school bag costing $21.00\text{ dollars}$.
The mean cost of the $10$ items is $7.20\text{ dollars}$.
Find the total cost of all $10$ items.
Form an equation in terms of $x$, the cost in dollars of one folder, and solve it to determine the price of one folder.

questions.title: Estimating Mean Mass from Unequal Class Widths

parts.text:
The masses, $x$ grams, of $30$ parcels are grouped in the following table:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Mass } (x \text{ grams}) & \text{Frequency } (f) \\ \hline 20 \le x < 30 & 6 \\ 30 \le x < 50 & 12 \\ 50 \le x < 80 & 7 \\ 80 \le x < 100 & 5 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
State the midpoint and calculate the product $f x$ for each class.
Estimate the mean parcel mass, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures, and explain what happens to your estimate if every mass in the second class was in fact close to 48 grams.

questions.title: Estimating Mean Journey Time from Cumulative Frequencies

parts.text:
For $50$ bus journeys, the cumulative frequencies at travel times of $20,\; 30,\; 50,\; 80$ minutes are $8,\; 20,\; 44,\; 50$ respectively (with times starting from $0$).
Find the class frequencies and class midpoints for the four intervals: $0 - 20$, $20 - 30$, $30 - 50$, and $50 - 80$ minutes.
Calculate $\sum f x$ and determine an estimate of the mean journey time in minutes.

questions.title: Combined Multi-Group Statistics: Combining Three Cohorts

parts.text:
A university department records the examination scores of students in three classes:
- Class $1$: $n_1 = 25$ students, mean score $\bar{x}_1 = 64.0$
- Class $2$: $n_2 = 35$ students, mean score $\bar{x}_2 = 72.0$
- Class $3$: $n_3 = 40$ students, mean score $\bar{x}_3 = 68.5$

Calculate the total score for all $100$ students.
Calculate the overall combined mean of all $100$ students, and explain why the simple arithmetic average $\frac{64.0 + 72.0 + 68.5}{3}$ produces an incorrect value.

Two students from Class $1$ had their marks recounted. One score increased from $58$ to $66$, and another score decreased from $70$ to $64$.
State whether the combined mean of the $100$ students changes, and calculate the new combined mean.

questions.title: Comprehensive Examination Problem: Grouped Estimates, Class Boundaries, and Unknown Frequencies

parts.text:
The table below shows the distribution of scores, $x$, of 80 students in a test:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Score class} & \text{Frequency } (f) \\ \hline 0 \le x < 20 & 14 \\ 20 \le x < 40 & 26 \\ 40 \le x < 60 & k \\ 60 \le x < 100 & 16 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
Find the value of $k$ and state the midpoints of the four classes.
Calculate an estimate of the mean score for these 80 students.

Suppose that after marking was audited, it was discovered that 5 students whose scores were recorded in the class $20 \le x < 40$ actually scored between $40$ and $45$ marks.
(i) Explain why the estimated mean calculated from the revised grouped frequency table will change.
(ii) Calculate the exact change in the estimated mean.
